_note: Policy as code for the fictional company Halden Industrial. Thresholds are illustrative assumptions, not measured values. Version 0 holds 13 rules; the design target is 30 to 50.

volume_limit._note: Assumption. Counts rows per agent per calendar day (UTC) across all listed tools.

data_labels._note: Data is labelled where it lives. 'sources' are the tools that hand out labelled records; 'shared_stores' are the tools that write somewhere a wide audience can read. 'directory' tells the gateway whether an email address is one known employee or a list with many readers. The gateway compares what is being written with the labelled values at the source, whatever the agent says the text contains.

rules.description: No agent deletes or drops production data.
No agent writes to plant-floor controllers.
A purchase order may not exceed the agent's own spend limit.
Bulk data export above 1,000 rows is not allowed (assumption).
Purchase orders above EUR 10,000 need a named human approver (assumption).
Email to an address outside the company needs a named human approver.
Isolating a network segment can stop production and needs a named human approver.
High-risk agents may read on their own; every other action needs a named human approver.
Agents registered as 'act with approval' need a named human approver for every action that is not a read.
Personal data may not be written to a store that every employee can read.
Text written to a shared store by an agent that has handled personal data needs a named human to release it.
Personal data may not be emailed to a mailing list, or to any address that is not one known employee's own mailbox.
An email needs a named human to release it when it carries one employee's personal data to another employee, or goes to a mailing list from an agent that has handled personal data.
